doc.title: Al Tinney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: Working at a behavioral center for young men
summary: Until age 70 he was a music instructor at a behavioral center dealing with fights.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Yeah. And I don’t want to do that. I waited to do this. I couldn’t wait long enough. I didn’t stop until I was 70 you know, and I was working at a behavioral center for young men and I found myself on the floor a few times, trying to break up fights and whatnot, and it was something for me to really get out of. I shouldn’t have been in it that long, not at 70 years old. But it was an enjoyable feat I’ll say, because I was supposed to be a music instructor, but different things would — you know how—

Yes. They used to have a saying, if it isn’t sex it’s violence. One comes out of the other. And you had some of that going on there — fights about whose mate is whose. So there wasn’t anything to be done about that. Go ahead.
